question: A patient is hospitalized for pneumonia. Gram-positive cocci in clusters are seen on sputum gram stain. Which of the following clinical scenarios is most commonly associated with this form of pneumonia?

options.opa: Elderly patient who has trouble swallowing and poor dentition
options.opb: HIV positive adult with a CD4 count less than 150 and an impaired diffusion capacity
options.opc: An otherwise healthy young adult with a week of mild fatigue, chills, and cough
options.opd: Hospitalized adult with development of pneumonia symptoms 2 weeks following a viral illness
options.ope: An alcoholic with evidence of empyema and "currant jelly sputum"

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Gram-positive cocci in clusters" -> "Staphylococcus aureus" -> "post-viral pneumonia" -> "hospitalized adult" -> "pneumonia symptoms 2 weeks following viral illness" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Gram-positive cocci in clusters" -> "Staphylococcus aureus" -> "aspiration pneumonia" -> "elderly patient" -> "trouble swallowing" -> "poor dentition" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Gram-positive cocci in clusters" -> "Staphylococcus aureus" -> "opportunistic infection" -> "HIV positive adult" -> "CD4 count less than 150" -> "impaired diffusion capacity" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Gram-positive cocci in clusters" -> "Staphylococcus aureus" -> "community-acquired pneumonia" -> "otherwise healthy young adult" -> "mild fatigue, chills, cough" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Gram-positive cocci in clusters" -> "Staphylococcus aureus" -> "empyema" -> "alcoholic" -> "currant jelly sputum" -> 40%
analysis: The presence of Gram-positive cocci in clusters on a sputum Gram stain is indicative of Staphylococcus aureus, which is commonly associated with post-viral pneumonia. This scenario is most likely to occur in a hospitalized adult who develops pneumonia symptoms following a viral illness, such as influenza.
